title: Grade 4 CHRISTIAN RELIGIOUS EDUCATION — 2.2 Zacchaeus the Tax Collector

pages.lesson:
PAGE 1: Overview

OVERVIEW
========

Luke 19:2-10 tells how Zacchaeus, a rich chief tax collector, climbed a tree to see Jesus. In this sub-strand you will retell that story, see how Zacchaeus changed, and learn to use money with integrity. You will also talk about why turning from sin matters if we want to be like Christ.

## Strand 2.0: The Holy Bible
Sub-strand 2.2: Zacchaeus the Tax Collector
Suggested lessons: 3

## Learning outcomes
By the end of the sub-strand, the learner should be able to:
a) retell the story of Zacchaeus
b) recount how Zacchaeus changed his behaviour positively
c) demonstrate integrity when using money
d) discuss why it is important to repent sins in order to be like Christ

## Key inquiry questions
1. How did Zacchaeus’ encounter with Jesus Christ change his behaviour?

## Core competencies
• Self-efficacy: the skill of expressing their emotions is exhibited as learners tell their friends how to turn away from bad behaviour/sin.

## Values
• Patriotism: they learn how Zacchaeus dedicated his life to serving his government regardless of the challenges his work posed to him and his family. He also pledged to give half his belongings to the poor and for anyone he had cheated he would pay back four times.

## Pertinent and contemporary issues
• Social Cohesion: learners carry out activities in groups such as singing.

## Links to other learning areas
• English: reading skills are applied as learners read the story of Zacchaeus.
• Creative Arts: creative skills are applied as learners draw, colour, role play and sing.

## Source
• KICD Grade 4 Christian Religious Education Curriculum Design (Revised 2024) — Strand 2.0 The Holy Bible, Sub-strand 2.2 Zacchaeus the Tax Collector
• Luke 19:2-10

PAGE 2: Lesson 1: The story of Zacchaeus

LESSON 1: THE STORY OF ZACCHAEUS
================================

## What you will learn
• Retell Luke 19:2-10 in the correct order.
• Name the people and the main actions in the story.

Curriculum outcomes: a) retell the story of Zacchaeus

## Introduction
Crowds can hide a short person. Zacchaeus wanted to see Jesus so much that he ran ahead and climbed a tree. What happened next changed him.

## Notes
The story is in Luke 19:2-10. Read it in turns so that every learner hears the words of the Bible.

### What the passage says
Zacchaeus was a chief tax collector, and he was wealthy. He wanted to see who Jesus was, but he was short and could not see over the crowd. He ran ahead and climbed a sycamore tree.

When Jesus reached the place, He looked up and told Zacchaeus to come down at once, because Jesus must stay at his house that day. Zacchaeus came down at once and welcomed Him gladly.

The people who saw this began to mutter. They said that Jesus had gone to be the guest of a sinner.

Zacchaeus stood up and said that he would give half of his possessions to the poor. He also said that if he had cheated anybody, he would pay back four times the amount.

Jesus said that salvation had come to that house that day, and that Zacchaeus too was a son of Abraham. Then Jesus said that the Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost.

### Keeping the order
A good retelling follows this order: Zacchaeus the rich chief tax collector; the crowd and the tree; Jesus calling him by name; the welcome; the crowd's complaint; the promise about money; Jesus' words about salvation. Do not add events that the passage does not tell. Draw Zacchaeus in the tree and share the drawing with a partner so the picture matches the reading.

## Key words
• tax collector — a person who collected taxes for the government
• chief tax collector — a leading tax collector, as Luke 19:2 describes Zacchaeus
• sycamore — the kind of tree Zacchaeus climbed so he could see Jesus

## Activity: Read and retell Luke 19:2-10
You will need: Bible, Pencils, Paper
1. Read Luke 19:2-10 in turns.
2. Close the Bible and retell the story in the correct order.
3. Draw and colour Zacchaeus on a tree.
4. Share the drawings with peers and check that they match the passage.

## Practice
1. What work did Zacchaeus do, and what does Luke 19:2 say about his wealth?
2. Why did Zacchaeus climb a sycamore tree?
3. What did Jesus say to Zacchaeus in the tree?

## Summary
• Zacchaeus was a rich chief tax collector who climbed a tree to see Jesus.
• Jesus called him and went to his house.
• Jesus said He came to seek and to save the lost.

### Answers to practice
1. He was a chief tax collector, and he was wealthy.
2. He was short and could not see Jesus over the crowd.
3. He told him to come down at once, because Jesus must stay at his house that day.

PAGE 3: Lesson 2: How Zacchaeus changed

LESSON 2: HOW ZACCHAEUS CHANGED
===============================

## What you will learn
• Recount how Zacchaeus changed his behaviour.
• Discuss why it is important to repent in order to be like Christ.

Curriculum outcomes: b) recount how Zacchaeus changed his behaviour positively; d) discuss why it is important to repent sins in order to be like Christ

## Introduction
Meeting Jesus did not leave Zacchaeus the same. He made promises about his money and the people he may have cheated. That change is what repentance looks like.

## Notes
Before Jesus called him, Zacchaeus was known as a sinner. The crowd said so when Jesus entered his house. Tax collectors in that time were often disliked because they could take more than they should. The passage itself shows Zacchaeus ready to put wrongs right.

### The change
Luke 19:8 records his new behaviour:

- He would give half of his possessions to the poor.
- If he had cheated anybody, he would pay back four times the amount.

He did not only feel sorry. He said what he would do. Jesus answered that salvation had come to that house. The Son of Man came to seek and to save the lost. Zacchaeus was one of the lost people Jesus came to save.

### Lessons from the story
- Jesus knows people by name and looks for the lost.
- No one is too disliked for Jesus to save.
- Repentance includes turning away from cheating.
- A saved person cares for the poor.
- Saying sorry is joined to putting things right.

### Why repent
To repent means to turn away from sin and turn to God. Christians want to be like Christ, who is honest, generous and merciful. If we keep a sin and will not turn, we are not following Him. Tell a friend one way to turn away from a bad habit: admit it, ask God for forgiveness, and do the right action instead. For Zacchaeus, the right action was giving to the poor and paying back four times what he had cheated.

Sing a song about Jesus Christ as the Saviour who seeks and saves the lost.

## Key words
• repent — to turn away from sin and turn to God
• salvation — being saved by Jesus, as He said had come to Zacchaeus' house
• Saviour — Jesus, who came to seek and to save the lost

## Activity: Lessons and a conversation about change
You will need: Bible, Exercise book
1. Read Luke 19:8-10 again.
2. State three lessons learnt from the story of Zacchaeus.
3. Tell a friend how to turn away from bad behaviour.
4. Discuss why repenting matters if we want to be like Christ.
5. Sing a song about Jesus Christ as the Saviour.

## Practice
1. What two promises did Zacchaeus make in Luke 19:8?
2. What did Jesus say had come to Zacchaeus' house?
3. Why is it important to repent?

## Summary
• Zacchaeus promised to give half of his possessions to the poor and to repay four times anyone he had cheated.
• Jesus said salvation had come to his house.
• Repentance means turning from sin so that we can be like Christ.

### Answers to practice
1. He would give half of his possessions to the poor, and if he had cheated anyone he would pay back four times the amount.
2. Salvation.
3. So that we turn from sin and become like Christ, who saves the lost.

PAGE 4: Lesson 3: Integrity when using money

LESSON 3: INTEGRITY WHEN USING MONEY
====================================

## What you will learn
• Explain integrity in the use of money.
• List ways of using money wisely, following Zacchaeus' example.

Curriculum outcomes: c) demonstrate integrity when using money

## Introduction
Money can be used to help or to cheat. Zacchaeus had become rich as a tax collector. After meeting Jesus, he chose honesty and generosity. That is integrity.

## Notes
Integrity means being honest right through, even when nobody is checking. With money, integrity means you do not take what is not yours, you do not cheat in a price or a tax, and you do what you said you would do.

### What Zacchaeus teaches about money
He did not say, "I will enjoy my wealth and forget the people." He said half of his possessions would go to the poor. He said cheating would be repaid four times. Four times is more than giving back the same amount. It shows he wanted to repair the harm fully.

He also kept serving. The story does not say he ran away from his work. It shows him putting right the wrongs that work had made possible. A person can do a hard job and still be honest.

### Ways to use money wisely
- Keep money that is yours. Return money that you find or that belongs to a friend.
- Do not cheat a buyer or a seller.
- Share with someone in need, as Zacchaeus promised to share with the poor.
- Pay back anything you took wrongly.
- Do not waste school fees or money a parent gave you for a set purpose.
- Give thanks to God for what you have, whether it is little or much.
- Write down what you spend so you remember where it went.

A learner shows integrity by refusing to steal a coin from a desk and by sharing lunch without boasting. Jesus saves people so that their money habits change too. Pray and ask Him to make you honest with every coin you hold.

## Key words
• integrity — honesty that stays the same even when nobody is watching
• possessions — the things a person owns
• generosity — willingness to give to others

## Worked examples

### Example 1
A shopkeeper's child is sent to buy bread and is given too much change. What would integrity look like?

Working:
1. The extra money is not his.
2. Zacchaeus promised to pay back what was wrongly taken.
3. The child should return the extra change.

Answer: He should return the extra money to the shopkeeper.

## Activity: List wise ways to use money
You will need: Exercise book
1. List ways of using money wisely.
2. Beside each way, say how it is like or unlike Zacchaeus after he met Jesus.
3. Role-play returning extra change and sharing with a classmate who has none.
4. Sing a song about Jesus the Saviour.

## Practice
1. What is integrity?
2. How did Zacchaeus show integrity with money?
3. Give two ways a learner can use money wisely.

## Summary
• Integrity means honesty even when nobody is watching.
• Zacchaeus gave to the poor and repaid cheating four times.
• Use money to help, not to cheat.

### Answers to practice
1. Being honest right through, even when nobody is watching.
2. He promised to give half of his possessions to the poor and to pay back four times anything he had cheated.
3. Any two: return what is not yours, do not cheat, share with the needy, pay back what you took, do not waste money given for a set purpose.
pages.quiz:
REVISION QUIZ — 2.2 ZACCHAEUS THE TAX COLLECTOR
========================================

Answer all the questions, then mark yourself on the Answers tab.

1. Where is the story of Zacchaeus found?
   A. Luke 19:2-10
   B. Genesis 1:1-25
   C. Judges 14:5-9
   D. Numbers 22:22-34

2. Zacchaeus was a...
   A. fisherman
   B. chief tax collector
   C. priest in the temple
   D. king of Moab

3. Why did he climb a tree?

4. What did the crowd say when Jesus went to Zacchaeus' house?
   A. They praised Zacchaeus for his honesty
   B. They muttered that Jesus was the guest of a sinner
   C. They asked Zacchaeus to be king
   D. They climbed the tree with him

5. Zacchaeus said he would give how much of his possessions to the poor?
   A. Nothing
   B. Half
   C. All of his house only
   D. One coin

6. If Zacchaeus had cheated anyone, he promised to pay back:
   A. the same amount
   B. twice the amount
   C. four times the amount
   D. nothing

7. Jesus said the Son of Man came to...

8. Why is repentance important for someone who wants to be like Christ?
   A. So they can keep cheating quietly
   B. So they turn from sin and follow Christ's ways
   C. So they can hide from Jesus
   D. So they become richer by any means

9. Integrity with money means...
   A. taking extra change and keeping quiet
   B. being honest even when nobody is watching
   C. counting other people's money in secret
   D. refusing to help the poor

10. Which action copies Zacchaeus' new behaviour?
   A. Keeping a coin you found in a friend's desk
   B. Returning what is not yours and sharing with someone in need
   C. Cheating a younger child in a game of money
   D. Hiding school fees
pages.answers:
ANSWERS — 2.2 ZACCHAEUS THE TAX COLLECTOR
========================================

1. A. Luke 19:2-10
   The class reads Luke 19:2-10.

2. B. chief tax collector
   Luke 19:2 says he was a chief tax collector and wealthy.

3. He was short and could not see Jesus because of the crowd.
   Luke 19:3-4 gives this reason.

4. B. They muttered that Jesus was the guest of a sinner
   Luke 19:7 says the people muttered that Jesus had gone to be the guest of a sinner.

5. B. Half
   Luke 19:8 says he would give half of his possessions to the poor.

6. C. four times the amount
   Luke 19:8 says he would pay back four times the amount.

7. Seek and save the lost.
   That is Luke 19:10.

8. B. So they turn from sin and follow Christ's ways
   Being like Christ means turning from sin, as Zacchaeus turned from cheating.

9. B. being honest even when nobody is watching
   Integrity is honesty that does not depend on being watched.

10. B. Returning what is not yours and sharing with someone in need
   Zacchaeus repaid wrong and gave to the poor.
